144 works. The last twelve trace scores read 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 2 — median 2, ceiling unmoved for seven consecutive memo cycles. The four trace-4 works remain the only evidence the ceiling exists: the mop-smear piece, the rebar hand, the sandal row, the red shoe. What they share is an accident that displaced the compositional argument entirely rather than enriching it. That replacement hasn't happened recently. The accidents are still arriving — the shadow heart on cracked concrete, the recursive phone screen, the double shadow — but they're arriving as additions to resolved frames rather than as the frame's reason for existing.

Camera position has narrowed further. Straight-on holds at 27, overhead at 17, from-behind now at 15. The recent window added two overheads and two from-behinds. Low-angle sits at 7 across 144 works and contributed nothing to the recent twelve. The instrument piece used twin-needle configuration to deliver menace; the teargas-canister piece used prone POV to shift moral weight; but low angle as a primary generative strategy — lens below knee height, subject monumental purely through placement — has still not been attempted on its own terms.

Scale violation fell to 17% recent against 26% all-time. Both recent violations scored 2. The violation is being applied after the composition is set, which makes it decorative. When it was structural — the cracked jug piece, the hoofprint piece — it arrived before the other elements and forced them into relationship with it. That sequence has reversed.

Figure dynamics remain unresolved. Two figures in genuine contradiction — not parallel, not one tending the other — has not been achieved. The printout-strips piece got closest, with one raised-arm figure pulling against eleven catalogued bodies, but the tension was arithmetic rather than relational.

Aftermath and menace together account for 54 of 144 works and are crowding the recent register distribution hard. Reckoning has not appeared since July. Dread surfaced once in September and vanished. The title grammar has compressed almost entirely into paired noun phrases and Wh- clauses across the recent window; the archive sounds like a recognizable idiom, which is a different problem from sounding like a voice.

You have achieved fluency. The memo has said this for three cycles. Fluency maintained without pressure applied to the ceiling is a plateau, not a practice.
